projects.vibe: A battle-tested Unix password manager that values stability, portability, and disciplined contribution over shiny new toys.
projects.highlight: Strict closed set of Conventional Commit types with explicit scoping rules for historical misuses.

projects.vibe: Merge at the entity, not the line — and make every refusal explain itself.
projects.highlight: Entity-level merge semantics: conflicts are resolved at function/class granularity, so independent edits to different functions never collide.

projects.vibe: Never crash, never panic, never copy — build a clean-room InDesign killer with paranoid Rust discipline.
projects.highlight: Crash prevention outranks feature work: no unwrap/expect/panic/unsafe in non-test code, with a last-resort panic guard for command execution and file I/O.

projects.vibe: Write code that reads like prose, test only what you own, and never let AI slop into the repo.
projects.highlight: Comments are treated as tech debt and banned unless they explain complex business logic, serve as tool input, or mark a TODO/FIXME with a reason.

projects.vibe: Deep invariant verification, strict typing, and defensive boundary guarantees.
projects.highlight: Agent Guidelines for open-code-review

projects.vibe: Treat every boundary as a contract, every failure as a signal, and every guess as a bug.
projects.highlight: Layered ESM TypeScript with strict inward-only dependency flow; provider protocols are forbidden in domain and application layers.

projects.vibe: Trust the source tree, not the prose — and never let an agent touch dist/ or hand-edit a snapshot.
projects.highlight: Explicit trust order: package.json scripts and the current source tree outrank prose docs, which may be stale.

projects.vibe: Ship focused commits, respect the guide, and never let agent artifacts pollute the repo.
projects.highlight: Single source of truth: the contribution guide owns shared rules; AGENTS.md and skills must not duplicate them.

projects.vibe: Ship cross-platform, cross-version, cross-host code that never lies about what it knows.
projects.highlight: Design system is linted, not suggested: raw palette colors, restyled primitives, and computed className strings fail CI.

projects.vibe: Deterministic task runners, disciplined formatting, and modular consistency.

projects.vibe: Readable code is a form of respect—for the next human and the next agent.
projects.highlight: Compile-time checked SQLx macros preferred over runtime queries

projects.vibe: A ruthless librarian for AI skills: every file has a place, every place has a rule, and no em-dash survives.
projects.highlight: Bucket taxonomy with strict promotion rules: engineering/ and productivity/ are promoted, misc/, in-progress/, and deprecated/ are not, and the boundary is enforced across README, plugin.json, and docs.

projects.vibe: Reuse ruthlessly, type precisely, comment sparingly — let the code speak.
projects.highlight: Mandates checking duckdb/ and src/ for existing implementations before writing new code, and refactoring to reuse when possible.

projects.vibe: If you didn't run it, don't paste it — and if you did, paste only that.
projects.highlight: A build is not a result: compiling and passing a self-test vector proves nothing about whether a mode actually cracks.

projects.vibe: Build fast, test hard, and never let a kernel sync without a benchmark.
projects.highlight: Strict language separation: Mojo for performance kernels, Python for orchestration.

projects.vibe: Treats GitHub as the source of truth and agents as disciplined workers, not planners.
projects.highlight: Coding agents act as workers within the contribution contract, not as a planning authority; GitHub holds the durable record.

projects.vibe: Protect the user's running app, verify scoped, and never let an agent touch what it hasn't earned.
projects.highlight: Hard prohibition on killing, relaunching, or replacing the user's running cmux.app, including via Release builds or bundle-ID collisions; CMUX_ALLOW_REPLACING_RUNNING_CMUX is user-only.

projects.vibe: The code is the contract, and every invariant is pinned by a test, a schema, or a grep.
projects.highlight: No separate spec: the emitted .d.ts, JSON schemas, and security tests are the three pinned contracts.

projects.vibe: Deterministic task runners, disciplined formatting, and modular consistency.
projects.highlight: Project Skills

projects.vibe: Guard the shared test kernel, prove the work ran, and never let a skill be optional when CI depends on it.
projects.highlight: Explicitly warns that Twig-only template changes must never get PHP integration tests, because rendering without a Storefront request can cache empty request-dependent Twig globals in the shared test kernel and break unrelated later tests.

projects.vibe: Infrastructure as Effects: type-safe, composable, and relentlessly correct.
projects.highlight: Infrastructure-as-Effects (IaE) framework that unifies business logic and infrastructure config into a single type-safe program.

projects.vibe: Map the repo, respect the contracts, run only what the task needs.
projects.highlight: Canonical source-of-truth discipline: edit SKILL.md first, then sync the .cursor mirror.

projects.vibe: Ship a plugin that installs cleanly everywhere, or don't ship at all.
projects.highlight: Ships-alone law: the published cadgen wheel must work in isolation, enforced by a boundary test that forbids references outside the package.

projects.vibe: One package per PR, no blank issues, no scanning the whole manifests tree — keep it surgical.
projects.highlight: Strict one-package-per-PR rule to keep changes reviewable and reversible.

projects.vibe: Keep the config authoritative, the layers thin, and the AI honest about what it doesn't know.
projects.highlight: Explicitly warns against copying rules into the file because 'copied versions, rule lists, and counts become stale' — a rare anti-duplication stance for agent docs.

projects.vibe: Event-sourced mobile navigation with a plugin-first, type-safe core.
projects.highlight: Event sourcing drives all state changes through domain events (Pushed, Popped, Replaced, etc.)

projects.vibe: Build less, verify precisely, and let the diff speak for itself.
projects.highlight: Verification is scoped to the change, not a ritual: no default package/Xcode/Tuist builds after every edit.

projects.vibe: Ship a self-hosted gym tracker with two dependencies and a test for every rep.
projects.highlight: Dependency-light is a hard constraint, not a preference: React + Router + Zustand on the frontend, two dependencies in the API.

projects.vibe: Kernel code is sacred: every line reviewed, every capability earned, every provider lie distrusted.
projects.highlight: The backend is the kernel — held to a higher bar, with every line read by reviewers, so diffs must stay small and elegant.

projects.vibe: Fight complexity, hit every surface, and never kill a process you didn't spawn.
projects.highlight: Explicit 'three ways to hurt yourself' section: no pkill by pattern, no writing to live userdata, no baking origins into dev bundles.

projects.vibe: Ship like a CEO, debug like a detective, and never let a green CI lie to you.
projects.highlight: 23 opinionated specialist skills that map to real org roles (CEO, Eng Manager, Designer, QA, Release) rather than generic 'assistant' personas.

projects.vibe: Security-first Go craftsmanship with strict module discipline and human-only community interactions.
projects.highlight: Module system is the architectural backbone: everything registers via caddy.RegisterModule() with namespaced IDs and lifecycle hooks.

projects.vibe: One file to rule them all — read the guide or don't bother.
projects.highlight: Single mandatory entry point: AGENT_GUIDE.md must be read before any response

projects.vibe: Skills are mandatory, personas don't talk to each other, and the user is always the orchestrator.
projects.highlight: Skill-first execution model: if a task matches a skill, you MUST invoke it — never implement directly.

projects.vibe: Ship the memory layer, skip the ceremony.
projects.highlight: Single build command (npm run build-and-sync) bundles build, marketplace sync, and worker restart into one atomic operation.

projects.vibe: Ship production-grade code through specialized agents, mandatory TDD, and zero tolerance for security shortcuts.
projects.highlight: 68 specialized agents mapped to every language, framework, and domain — from Rust to healthcare compliance

projects.vibe: Multi-agent-safe, type-strict, no-fluff engineering with explicit guardrails for every destructive action.
projects.highlight: Multi-session git safety: only stage files you changed, never `git add -A`, never `git reset --hard` or `--no-verify`.

projects.vibe: Precision over brute force: run the narrowest test that proves your change, never the whole suite.
projects.highlight: Validation is mapped to change type via a table, enforcing the narrowest possible test scope.

projects.vibe: Monorepo discipline: virtualenvs, scoped AGENTS.md files, and never leak a customer slug into git history.
projects.highlight: AGENTS.md files are declared the single source of truth for AI agent instructions, explicitly forbidding duplication into CLAUDE.md or Cursor rules.

projects.vibe: Ship skills like software: versioned, tested, and cross-agent compatible.
projects.highlight: Two-layer versioning system with strict rules: repo release (x.y.z) and per-skill metadata.version, both CI-enforced.

projects.vibe: Why use many token when few token do trick — but route every repo like a paranoid monorepo architect.
projects.highlight: Binding cross-repo routing table: each concern (skills, Engine, MV3 extension, Agent SDK, Browse driver, Pebble) has exactly one owning repository.

projects.vibe: Glue, don't rewrite — route cleanly, test everything, and never touch upstream code.
projects.highlight: Explicit positioning as installer/doctor/config tool, not a wrapper — agents call upstream tools directly after install

projects.vibe: Deterministic graphs, surgical edits, and a single source of truth for every agent.
projects.highlight: Extraction is deterministic — derived from AST, not LLM-summarized.
